plugin.body: A plugin is a folder here with a plugin.json: it declares agents sessions can run on, and may speak — a process of its own the driver asks before a start and tells of an ending. No code from a plugin ever runs inside Daoris.
plugin.none: No plugins — copy a folder in with `daoris plugin add <folder>`.
plugin.removeConfirm: Removes its folder from this machine. What it kept stays at `{{data}}`, yours to delete.
plugin.enabled: {{id}} is on. The driver asks it from its next look.
plugin.disabled: {{id}} is off. It stays where it is; the driver stops asking it at its next look.
plugin.removedKept: {{id}} is removed from this machine. What it kept is still at {{data}}.
plugin.terminal: Also `daoris plugin list|add|update|remove|enable|disable` — the same folder and the same file, either door.
plugin.source.offer: Installed from Daoris's own plugins, which this install carries.
plugin.source.none: No record of where it came from: it was added before Daoris kept one, or copied in by hand, so there is nothing to update it from. Adding it again with `daoris plugin add <folder>` records it.
plugin.source.unread: Its record of where it came from does not read: {{problem}}
plugin.update.title: What an update changes
plugin.update.same: What it declares does not change; its files are replaced from where it came from.
plugin.update.note: Update now replaces its folder whole, and what it kept stays. Nothing starts at the press: the driver starts it again at its next look.
plugin.update.done: {{id}} is updated. What it kept stayed, and the driver starts it again at its next look.
plugin.offers.title: Daoris's own plugins
plugin.offers.body: Plugins this install carries and this machine has not installed. Nothing of one runs until you install it, and one that lands work runs only where a workspace's landing rule names it.
plugin.offers.needs: What it needs, set up by you:
plugin.offers.installed: {{id}} is installed. The driver reads it at its next look; a plugin that lands work runs only where a landing rule names it.
plugin.offers.terminal: Also `daoris plugin add --offer <id>` — the same copy, either door; `daoris plugin list` shows what this install offers.
plugin.kit.title: Make a plugin
plugin.kit.body: A plugin is code that runs on this machine as you, so making one is work: a folder in a repository of yours, with its tests, reviewed before anyone installs it. New writes that folder — a manifest, a wire script answering each point, its wire test and a README — and installs nothing. Try starts a plugin as the driver would and checks every answer by the driver's own reader.
plugin.kit.kind.decision: A decision, before a planned start spends anything
plugin.kit.kind.observation: An observation, after a session ends
plugin.kit.kind.act: An act, once a landing has made its branch
plugin.kit.folderPlaceholder: a folder in your plugins repository
plugin.kit.folderHint: The plugin's own folder is made inside this one and named by its id. A folder that already holds anything is refused, never written over.
plugin.kit.made: Made {{id}} in {{folder}}: its manifest, wire script, wire test and README. Run node --test there, then try it.
plugin.kit.tryHint: Starts it with the driver's own frames, the repository in each an empty folder with no git behind it. What it keeps goes to a scratch folder, removed after.
plugin.kit.working: Trying — as long as the driver would wait for an answer, up to two minutes for a landing.
plugin.kit.terminal: Also `daoris-driver plugins new|try` — the same kit, either door. In a plugins repository with no Daoris, `node --test` runs the wire test the kit wrote.
